# Backlog — done (archive)

Rows that have landed, newest first. Split out of [BACKLOG.md](BACKLOG.md) by
**A8**, 2026-08-12, when that file reached 76 KB and every run on three machines
was reading all of it to find the handful of rows it could act on.

**Rows here are verbatim** — archiving never rewrites one. A row arrives here
only when its work has *landed*: `IN-REVIEW` means the PRs are open, `DONE`
means they merged. Flipping a row and moving it is a STEP 4 chore, described in
[BACKLOG.md](BACKLOG.md).

This file is history, not queue. An agent picking work reads
[BACKLOG.md](BACKLOG.md); come here for precedent — how a past stage was
verified, what a previous run measured, why a decision went the way it did.

| E61 | 2026-08-28 | any | **A TEXT EDIT OUTLIVES THE MODULE IT IS EDITING, AND CRASHES ON COMMIT. USE-AFTER-FREE, reproduced by Jeff 2026-08-28 (macos, interactive) as soon as **E57** made keyboard delete work:** *"crash after deleting outer and editing pin name (of it's child)"*. **THE STACK NAMES IT EXACTLY:** `PropertiesBrowser::Body()::$_13(std::string const&)` <- `GMPI_MAC_TextEdit::dismissTextField(gmpi::ReturnCode)` <- `-[NSTextField textDidEndEditing:]`, `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` / `SIGSEGV`, `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS` with a pointer-authentication failure -- the signature of a call through freed memory rather than a null. **A pin-name field was open on a child module; deleting the child's container freed it; the still-live `NSTextField`'s completion lambda then fired on end-editing and dereferenced its stale capture.** **THIS IS NOT E47, AND E47 IS INNOCENT.** The same run proves [SynthEditLib#64](https://github.com/JeffMcClintock/SynthEditLib/pull/64)'s guard WORKS: probes caught it reaching `sender == layoutContainer` (`0x1055c07a0` both) with `currentModule` the live child `0x7d3084700`, and clearing it to `0x0`. **`currentModule` is correctly null. The crash is through a DIFFERENT pointer** -- one captured in a lambda handed to the platform text edit. **THE TWO SYMPTOMS ARE CAUSALLY LINKED, which is the part worth keeping.** #64 deliberately CLEARS WITHOUT INVALIDATING -- its comment says *"a repaint driven from inside a destructor is more than removing a dangling pointer requires"*. Defensible for the pointer, but the pane then keeps DISPLAYING the dead child's fields, and **that is what hands the user a live control over freed memory.** Jeff saw it first as *"deleting the outer container with the keyboard leaves the properties pane showing it's child"* -- which reads cosmetic and is not. **Scope** `SynthEditLib/EditorLib/PropertiesBrowser.cpp` -- the `Body()` lambdas and whatever owns the live text edit -- **GATED**. Two candidate shapes, and the choice wants measuring rather than guessing: dismiss/cancel any open text edit when `currentModule` is cleared, or make the completion lambda capture something that can be validated (a handle re-resolved through the document, as `ug_patch_param_setter` does) instead of a raw pointer. **Accept** with a pin-name field open on a module, delete that module's container: the edit is dismissed or its commit is refused, no fault, and the pane no longer renders the freed module. **Size** small if dismissing the edit is enough; medium if every `Body()` capture has to be re-keyed. |

Full write-up with every call chain: [docs/e9-sample-rate.md](docs/e9-sample-rate.md).** Jeff asked how SynthEdit's AU and VST3 targets handle a rate change, on the premise that it requires rebuilding the DSP graph. **The premise is right and the rebuild already exists** — `SynthRuntime::prepareToPlay` rebuilds when `generator->SampleRate() != sampleRate` (`SynthEditLib/SynthRuntime.cpp:51`), and every format wrapper drives it. **What is wrong is "the rack would keep the stale rate and everything detuned".** A rate change is absorbed by *destroying the `IProcessor` and constructing a new one*: `gmpi_processor::start_processor` (`GMPI/Hosting/processor_holder.cpp:48`) releases the old plugin at `:55`, creates a fresh instance at `:69`, calls `open()` at `:82`, and **deliberately re-seeds the blob parameter from its retained bytes** (`:215`), so TIDE's chunk arrives again, `onSetPins` fires again, and the rack is built at the NEW rate. Triggers: VST3 `setActive(true)` (`Processor_VST3.cpp:369`, and the spec MANDATES the `setActive(false)` → `setupProcessing(newRate)` → `setActive(true)` bracket, `ivstaudioprocessor.h:307`); AU `Initialize()` (`AU2_Wrapper.cpp:483`, with `StreamFormatWritable` returning false while initialised at `:978` so the host MUST `Uninitialize` first); CLAP `activate()` (`Processor_CLAP.cpp:366`); standalone `onAudioFormatChanged` (`StandaloneHost.cpp:405`). **`gmpi::api::IProcessor` has three methods — `open`, `setBuffer`, `process` (`GMPI/Core/GmpiApiAudio.h:50`) — so there is nowhere to put a rate-change callback; the rate is PULLED via `getSampleRate()`.** **Measured in REAPER on `tests/hosts/v3-midi-pitch.rpp`**, driving Preferences → Audio → Device → Request sample rate 48000 → 44100 → 48000 by hand on the loaded project: eight `TIDE: rack built for N Hz` lines, the rate following the device each time, and playback after the change metering **−6.2 dBFS peak / −13.4 RMS** — the same level the fixture gives at 48 kHz. **Not one line carried the `(rate CHANGED)` suffix, and it never can:** `preparedSampleRate` is a member of the object `start_processor` destroys, so the guard cannot outlive the rebuild that handles the change. The repeated identical `44100` lines prove it — a surviving instance with an unchanged rate prints nothing. **What is LEFT of this row, and it is smaller and different:** (1) **a fresh instance with no chunk stored never prepares at all** — `processor_holder.cpp:225` `continue`s on an empty blob and TIDE's only `prepareToPlay` call site is that blob arriving; the fix is to override `open()` exactly as SynthEdit's own glue does (`se_gmpi/source/SeGmpiProcessor.cpp:151`) and let the blob be a pure document swap; (2) `DoAsyncRestart()` alone CANNOT absorb a rate change — the `resetting` branch rebuilds from the member `sampleRate` (`SynthRuntime.cpp:388`) which only `prepareToPlay` writes (`:33`), and those members are non-atomic, written outside `generatorLock`, read on the audio thread; (3) `prepareToPlay` never joins `dspBuilderThread`, so its precondition is the wrappers' own — no concurrent `process()`. **Two comments in `SynthEditSem/SynthEdit.cpp` were wrong and are fixed with this research:** the stale-rate inference above, and *"the AsyncRestart path is unreachable in the plugin runtime"* — `resetting` is reached via `ug_vst_out.h:65` → `SeAudioMaster::onFadeOutComplete()` → `OnFadeOutComplete()` (`iseshelldsp.h:124`), and `DoAsyncRestart` is reached from `dsp_patch_parameter.cpp:773` for any host control with `requiresAsyncRestart()`, a set that **includes `HC_PATCH_CABLES`** (`dsp_patch_parameter_base.h:187`), i.e. every rack re-cabling. Nothing in TIDE calls it *yet*, which is a property of TIDE's wiring, not of the runtime. **Unmeasured, deliberately not claimed:** AU and CLAP, because TIDE builds neither (`SynthEditSem/CMakeLists.txt:59` is `GMPI VST3 STANDALONE`); and whether parsing a document on the audio thread is safe. **Original item, kept for the record:** **TIDE latches its sample rate at DOCUMENT-PUSH time and has no rate-change path — found 2026-08-18 (macos, interactive) when Jeff asked whether TIDE has the correct sample rate or a hard-coded default.** **It is NOT hard-coded**, which was the first thing checked: `SynthEditSem/SynthEdit.cpp` passes `static_cast<int32_t>(host->getSampleRate())` to `rack.prepareToPlay`, and a temporary log confirmed real values arriving from REAPER — **48000 Hz** and **44100 Hz**, block 512. **The problem is WHERE that call lives:** `prepareToPlay` is reached from exactly one place, the chunk arriving in `onSetPins`, so the rack's rate is fixed when the DOCUMENT is pushed. Nothing in the class handles a rate change. **A host that changes rate without re-pushing the document would leave the rack at the stale rate and everything detuned by the ratio — silently, with no warning and nothing in the saved project to show it.** 48000 → 44100 is 1.47 semitones, so it would sound wrong rather than broken, which is the worst kind. **What is measured and what is not, kept apart deliberately:** an offline render prints both rates, but those are two separate plugin **INSTANCES** (the device/editor one and the render one), each latching once at construction — the guard's "rate CHANGED" branch did **not** fire, which is how that is known rather than assumed. So a rate change *within* an instance has never been observed to be handled, and on this evidence it would not be. **A rate-change test needs the GUI:** REAPER ignores a project's `SAMPLERATE` line when rendering, and hand-writing `RENDER_SRATE` into a `.rpp` makes REAPER stop on a dialog (confirmed by Jeff while it blocked a render), so forcing a different render rate has to go through REAPER's own dialog. **Scope** `SynthEditSem/SynthEdit.cpp` — TIDE's own, ALLOWED. A `preparedSampleRate` guard is already in place and logs `TIDE: rack built for N Hz` on a change; what is missing is acting on it. **Accept** changing the host's sample rate on a loaded project re-tunes correctly rather than staying detuned. **Size** small if a rate check per block is acceptable; larger if it wants a proper host callback. **NOT the cause of E8:** that offset is exactly 3 semitones (ratio 1.18921), a musical interval and not any standard rate ratio — 48000/44100 is 1.47 semitones — and the Oscillator's 5 V → 440.0 Hz holds at both 44100 (via the `.rpp`) and 48000 (via E1's `prefab_oscillator`). |

So the shipped artifact's identity is a pure function of that string. `Factory_CLAP.cpp:25` assigns the same string straight to `clap_descriptor.id`, and GMPI uses it as the id directly. **Measured, not inferred:** a CLAP host handshake reports `id="SE SynthEdit" name="TIDE Rack" vendor="TIDE Synth"` — see [tests/e9_clap_rate_probe.c](tests/e9_clap_rate_probe.c). **What breaks:** any other GMPI plugin declaring that id gets the SAME VST3 GUID and the SAME CLAP id, so a host with both installed cannot tell them apart and a saved project can reload the wrong one.
